actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

facts.text: MJPC is an interactive application and software framework for real-time predictive control with MuJoCo, developed by Google DeepMind
MJPC supports multiple shooting-based planners: iLQG and Gradient Descent are derivative-based and Predictive Sampling is derivative-free
An MJPC task needs an MJCF file that describes the simulated model and the task parameters and a C++ file that implements the residual
The Fingers task loads fingers/task.xml from XmlPath and is named FreeFingers
The Fingers task is registered in the MJPC task list
The task XML's root model is named 'Free-Floating Fingers'
The task XML includes ../common.xml, the shared visual assets and materials
The model integrates with timestep 0.001 s, an elliptic friction cone, five noslip iterations and the implicit integrator
The object and target bodies each have a free joint and a box geom; the object's collision default class sets mass 0.2 and its visual class mass 0.001
The finger_a and finger_b bodies each have three slide joints along x, y and z
The six intvelocity actuators A_x, A_y, A_z, B_x, B_y and B_z each have ctrlrange -.99 to .99, ctrllimited true and kp 1000; the x and y actranges are -1 to 1 and the z actranges 0 to 1.4
The home keyframe holds 20 qpos values (two free joints of 7 and six slides) and 6 act values
The sensors are the user sensors Reach (dim 6), Bring (dim 3) and Control (dim 6), plus framepos sensors for both fingers, the object and the six sites
The Fingers residual subtracts each finger's position from the object's, writes the distance of three object sites to their target sites, and copies data->ctrl for each of model->nu actuators

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF for the six actuator control ranges, the qpos/qvel dimensions and the 0.001 s step, but it integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated slide joint toward its control target and resolves no contact, friction, inertia, equality, tendon, actuator or sensor dynamics
the two free bodies (object and target) are not integrated and no mesh or texture is loaded by the stand-in; the floor, the box geoms and the site geometry are not resolved
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

the MJPC task layer is not served: the C++ Fingers residual (fingers.cc:34-54), the custom task settings of task.xml:7-18, the planners and the GUI are outside this driver, which exposes the raw ctrl vector and the MuJoCo integration state
the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData, so the model defaults are restored, not the home keyframe of task.xml:20-34
the stand-in implements no mj_getState/mj_setState, so a snapshot uses the bridge's fallback time/qpos/qvel/act/ctrl copy rather than the full integration state; it was not compared with the engine
no rendering, camera or image is produced, and no physical device is modelled or was validated

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
